biography.plain_text: Fabrice Vial was a French industrialist who expanded his family's joinery business into Vial Menuiseries, a discount producer and retailer of doors, windows and staircases. Based in Portugal, he retained a controlling stake in the listed group. Its growth made him wealthy and supported his later investments in French yacht construction.

confidence.reason: Primary equity records and contemporary reporting support the identity card.

long_biography.plain_text:
Fabrice Vial's expertise in purchasing helped shape his joinery group's industrial strategy. When its main supplier raised prices after a takeover, the business began making its own products. Factories in France, Spain and Romania reduced dependence on outside suppliers and gave the group greater control over quality and delivery times.

Using his own capital, he acquired the struggling Couach shipyard, committing to retain its workforce. His plan combined large yacht construction with repair work at Saint-Mandrier, where expanded facilities would accommodate vessels over fifty metres. He backed the existing shipbuilding teams and sought fresh orders to sustain production.
